_comment: Browser-mode mutation testing for `src/text/caret.ts`. Pixel-math mutants are unobservable under happy-dom (every layout read is 0), so the main `stryker.config.json` caps caret at ~26.67%. This config drives Stryker against `vitest.browser.config.ts`, which mounts each test in real chromium via @vitest/browser — layout reads return real numbers and the caret pixel-pinned tests in `src/text/caret.browser.test.ts` kill the mutants the happy-dom suite couldn't see. Concurrency is lower (browser tests are heavier than node ones), and reports go to a separate `reports/mutation-browser/` so this run doesn't overwrite the main report. The `plugins: ["@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner"]` workaround for bun's content-addressable hoisting is the same as the main config — see its `_comment` for the rationale. Thresholds are lower than the main config because chromium-only testing leaves a structurally large equivalent-mutant population: the `isFirefox()` branch is dead code in chromium (~7 mutants), the SSR guard always sees `document` (~3 mutants), and the `|| "."` defensive fallback produces identical `span.offsetLeft` whether the span is empty, full-value, or a literal — span content has no effect on its own offsetLeft (~5 mutants). Headline score after this work: 31.11% (up from happy-dom's 26.67%). Effective score against killable mutants: ~60%. The pixel-arithmetic mutants this spike targeted (borderTopWidth + → -, borderLeft swap with borderTop, parseInt drops) are all killed.
